Existing guarantees hold: edge wrap, no one-tile stubs, ladder gauges, menu demo, run receipts and leaderboard fairness (or a documented migration).
Headless phone screenshots at several levels show the board fitting the viewport without clipping, checked and described.

text: Owner request 2026-11-15: make tiles slightly smaller so 2 to 5 more tiles fit across and down, and grow the board as progression gets harder so mazes can be longer and more complex.

acceptanceCriteria: A written research note cites sources on maze generation algorithms and measurable difficulty (solution length, branching, dead-end depth, decision density) and says which fit Mazer.
The note proposes an endless curve: what grows (board size, branching, deception, solution length), how it is measured per generated maze, and what stops it plateauing.
The proposal respects the owner direction on obstacles and enemies being decided one by one later, and lists what it needs from those cards.
A first build slice is named with tests, ready as a follow-up card.

text: Owner request 2026-11-15: research how to build genuinely harder mazes and an endless progression engine that never plateaus; deliver a researched design and the first build slice.

Merged: the menu demo now has its own profile with bleed-off paths restored (about 4 openings at level 20-30, about 15 at level 60, about 19 at 100 and up); real levels and ladder untouched and pinned by a test. Headless only; density at level 100 and up may be too heavy, one clamp dials it down.

Research done (report on file, 18 sources): difficulty today is capped by the fixed board (scale 35, about 25x49 tiles), geometry stops rising at level 288; a smaller tile scale of 38 to 40 gives 2 to 5 more tiles across and 4 to 10 more down on phones with a 10 px tile floor; truly endless needs a camera on a board bigger than the screen. Build slices S0 to S5 planned.
Building slices S0 (calibration table) and S1/S2 (scale 38 growing to 40 by level, 10 px tile floor) first; camera for endless play and leaderboard policy await Zac.

Centre dot on maze tiles removed and merged (bake version bumped). The thin white line before the reveal is not isolated: it looks like the 1px rim of the first faint tiles showing before their dark fill; it will be fixed as part of the new build and tear-down animation (MOTION-020), so it stays open.

Owner decisions: tile floor 10 px yes; no camera or zoom yet, the board stays fully on screen with only a slight size increase; difficulty rise by the felt-plus-density ladder; no leaderboard reset and no reset of anyone's current level; breather levels not added.

Changes ship behind the felt-plus-density ladder slice with tests, and no player level or leaderboard entry is reset.
Headless phone screenshots of before and after mazes are looked at and described.
new.description: Use the existing generator features together so mazes read as real mazes: long winding routes, many believable dead ends, branching, deception and a clear start-to-finish journey, growing with level.

text: Owner request 2026-11-15: research how to build genuinely harder mazes and an endless progression engine that never plateaus; deliver a researched design and the first build slice.
Deferred: this card duplicates MAZER-UI-029 (retire the future-phaser path), so it is parked and UI-029 carries the work.

Audit done (report and contact sheets on file): levels 10 to 100 read as a comb or circuit board, not a real maze (straight spines, blank areas, short local routes, straight wrap corridors); levels 200 and up look like real mazes. Cause: fill and felt targets are fixed cell counts tuned on the old board. Prototype (not shipped) fixes fill and blank areas. Plan: board-aware targets with the board-size slices, then longer start-to-goal routes and turning branches. Generation time on bigger boards must be measured with the repo harness before shipping.
